provenance.notes: EUR-Lex's pages (legal notice, data-reuse help, the text of Decision 2011/833/EU) could not be read on 2026-11-10: the site answers automated fetches with a challenge (HTTP 202, empty body). The licence follows Commission Decision 2011/833/EU on the reuse of Commission documents, which adopted CC BY 4.0 in 2019 (as search results summarised it; not read at the source); the credit text is EUR-Lex's usual wording, not re-read. Documents the Commission cannot license (third-party rights, documents received from other institutions) are outside it. Read the same day: the Publications Office's copyright notice (op.europa.eu), which sends reuse questions on Cellar to op-copyright@publications.europa.eu. This package calls the Cellar SPARQL endpoint (publications.europa.eu/webapi/rdf/sparql) and resources under publications.europa.eu/resource/: no published rate limit or usage terms were found for them; a test call carried no rate-limit header.
